- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (especially if sentiment drops post-spike) — adjust downward bias.
- Overshoot near end of forecast horizon (especially days 25–30) — apply mean reversion correction.
- Lagged sentiment (e.g., 3–5 days prior) strongly influences direction — align forecast slope with sentiment trend.
- When sentiment is low (< 0.3), avoid upward bias — forecast should trend downward or flat.
- If forecast starts high and true outcome dips sharply, reduce early forecast values by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.
- For multi-day forecast horizons, smooth transitions between sentiment peaks and troughs — avoid abrupt jumps.
- If sentiment is rising but price is falling, reduce forecast slope — sentiment may not fully reflect price momentum.
- Correct for “sentiment lag” — if sentiment peaks 2–3 days before price spike, forecast should anticipate it earlier.
